newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Old debt hitch surfaces in Yugo-Czech deal-Tanjug.
newsitem.headline: Old debt hitch surfaces in Yugo-Czech deal-Tanjug.

text.p: A deal may be concluded in the next few days on the first $62 million tranche of a credit by Czech bank Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. to Serbia's power company Elektroprivreda Srbije (EPS), Tanjug news agency said on Wednesday.
But the Belgrade news agency quoted financial experts as saying that problems had emerged in the loan talks over old debts EPS owes to Czech engineering group Skoda a.s..
The latest deal is aimed at putting into operation a commercial arrangement signed in April under which the Czech bank will finance Skoda equipment for the Yugoslav thermal power plant Kolubara B.
If the Czech bank failed to sign the agreement, EPS and Skoda would have to find other sources to finance Czech equipment for the 700 MegaWatt power plant, said Tanjug
Although the size of the old debts had been agreed, Serbian financial experts insisted that new business deals could not be dependent on old debt repayment, said Tanjug.

Yugoslavia is waiting to conclude deals with international financial institutions which will represent a framework for any old debt repayment, but only after Belgrade is readmitted to the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
The cost on the work on Kolubara B is estimated at $452 million by the year 2000, of which $65 million is needed in 1997.
